identity.title: Exact Functional ANOVA Decomposition for Categorical Inputs Models

problem.claim: Define an exact Functional ANOVA decomposition for categorical inputs under arbitrary feature dependence.

gap.claim: General dependent distributions lacked explicit closed-form decompositions, leading practitioners to use costly sampling-based approximations.

contributions.claim: Derives a closed-form categorical-input decomposition by combining functional analysis with an extension of discrete Fourier analysis, without distributional assumptions.
Extends the decomposition to arbitrary dependence structures, including non-rectangular support, while recovering the classical independent case.
Provides a natural generalization of SHAP values to the general categorical setting via the SHAP–ANOVA link under independence.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their framework completely resolves the closed-form limitation for categorical inputs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the formulation is computationally very efficient.
The authors report that the formulation recovers the classical independent case and handles arbitrary dependence, including non-rectangular support.

narrative_sequence.summary: Functional ANOVA is presented as a decomposition of predictions into main effects and higher-order interactions, with strong connections to SHAP for independent features.
For general dependent distributions, the absence of a closed form has led to costly sampling-based approximations.
The paper derives a closed-form decomposition for categorical inputs using functional analysis and discrete Fourier analysis.
The formulation is reported as efficient, compatible with the independent case, applicable to arbitrary dependence, and useful for generalizing SHAP values.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects the proposed general formulation to a familiar special case and to a related interpretability quantity, SHAP.

lessons.interpretation: Anchoring a generalization in established limiting cases and related concepts can make its scope easier to assess.
lessons.application: When presenting a new decomposition, explicitly state which classical case it recovers and how it relates to existing attribution measures.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no meaningful special case or well-defined relation to prior quantities exists.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the decomposition formula, computational complexity, categorical-domain assumptions, or details supporting the efficiency claim.
No concrete runtime comparison, sampling baseline, or empirical evaluation is reported in the supplied units.
The abstract does not specify the theorem or proof conditions underlying the stated generality.
